applicability: A build succeeds but a buffer overflow, a missing pipeline stage, or a generated-code edge is suspected.
A tile is flagged by PH001 or a pipeline depth is reduced by PH-MR-001.
Printed IR, pass snapshots, or build reports must be inspected without guessing from the Python source.
directions: Compile with `RunConfig(dump_passes=PassDumpLevel.EXPLICIT)` and inspect `passes_dump/NN_after_SomePass.py` when a pass decision matters.

Read `report/memory_after_AllocateMemoryAddr.txt` for Mat/Acc/Vec occupancy and `report/perf_hints.log` for PH001 and PH-MR-001 before changing a tile or stage, using the default planner where that report exists.
Use `python -m pypto.tools.memory_map` on a pass dump to see liveness and headroom; do not expect it to work under PTOAS.
Use `compile()` rather than `lower()` when code generation is the thing being validated.
effects: Per-pass snapshots make compiler behavior observable but consume disk and can be large.
The memory report is exact for the build but not a runtime measurement.
Address-dependent artifacts are useful under the default planner but unavailable when PTOAS owns address assignment.
invariants: `lower()` performs no code generation and writes no artifacts; a pass-only check can miss a codegen failure.
`compiled.program` is the specialized pre-pass program, not the final lowered IR.
With the default PYPTO planner, read the address-report file. PTOAS skips address assignment, so address-dependent memory-map rendering is unavailable.
Generated build artifacts are diagnostics, not source of truth; do not hand-edit generated orchestration or treat it as the fix.
principle: PyPTO's IR is immutable and SSA, so passes build new IR and per-pass snapshots are meaningful. `lower()` runs the configured pass pipeline and returns post-pass IR; `compile()` additionally performs code generation and writes artifacts. `compiled.program` retains the specialized pre-pass program, not the pass output. `compile(..., config=RunConfig(dump_passes=PassDumpLevel.EXPLICIT))` writes a snapshot after every pass; `lower()` never writes pass snapshots. With the default PYPTO planner, every build writes `build_output/<case>/report/memory_after_AllocateMemoryAddr.txt`, which reports each compute function's `Mat`, `Left`, `Right`, `Acc`, and `Vec` usage against limits. Under PTOAS, `AllocateMemoryAddr` is skipped, so do not expect address-dependent artifacts to answer the same question. Every compile also writes `report/perf_hints.log`: PH001 flags a `tile.load` or `tile.store` whose innermost dimension is below the backend's transfer granularity with the exact source location and bytes moved; PH-MR-001 reports a software-pipelining depth that was reduced by capacity and recommends shrinking the per-stage tile or lowering `stage=`. The memory report is authoritative over hand estimates because it includes alignment, allocator padding, liveness overlap, and backend transforms. `pypto.tools.memory_map` renders an allocation lifetime map from a pass dump: compile with `dump_passes=PassDumpLevel.EXPLICIT`, then run `python -m pypto.tools.memory_map <passes_dump/NN_after_SomePass.py> -o map.html`. Read it for tiles alive longer than necessary and for headroom for another pipeline stage or cross-core ring. Generated build artifacts are regenerated by compilation; inspect them as diagnostics only and make source fixes through public APIs.
questions: Whether the local toolchain's dump-pass API and `pypto.tools.memory_map` are available under the installed PyPTO 0.1.0 package was not checked.
risks: Using `lower()` as the final validation and missing a ptoas or codegen rejection.
Reading a memory-map dump from PTOAS and concluding there are no buffers because no addresses are assigned.
Treating a build-time memory report as a runtime measurement.
Assuming PH001's 512-byte threshold applies unchanged to every backend.
summary: The compiler exposes its decisions through pass dumps, a memory report, a perf-hint log, a memory-map viewer, and generated artifacts. Use those artifacts to distinguish a tile-shape problem from a liveness problem and a codegen problem from a runtime problem, without editing generated code.
title: Pass Dumps, Memory Maps, Perf Hints, and Compiler Diagnostics
